summary: Instagram is where nearly all the audience is: most videos get 500-1,400 views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly get under 60 views. The best videos make a bold 'X doesn't do what you think' claim about a familiar gadget (clap switch, gyro robot, mic) and use a personal, relatable or funny angle. Generic 'How does X work? 🤔' titles, the English video, and the newest sensor-spec videos (soil, TDS, CO2, geyser) get little reach and almost no shares or saves.
winningPattern: Hindi, Instagram-first videos about a familiar gadget or robot, with a surprising contradiction hook ('X can't do Y, it only does Z' or 'without X the robot falls'). Titles are short, in Hinglish, with one emoji, and the topic is visual and relatable (clap switch, balancing robot, mic, UV sunburn). The top shares came from everyday-life myths (sunburn on cloudy days), and saves came from robot and clap-switch explainers.
doMore: Make Instagram the primary platform and post there first; treat YouTube as a secondary repost
Open with a myth-busting or 'what happens without it' hook about a gadget people already know
Build series on the proven themes: clap switch, robots (gyro, line follower, IR), mic/speaker, and everyday-life myths like UV and sunburn
Add a share trigger, such as 'send this to the friend who believes X', since myth topics get shares and saves
Remake the strongest ideas with a new angle, for example a clap switch part 3 or a gyro robot demo
stopDoing: Generic 'Kaise kaam karta hai? 🤔' titles with no surprising claim
Posting dry component-spec topics (TDS, CO2, geyser thermocouple, soil sensor) with no relatable hook or demo
Publishing English or YouTube-only videos, since they got almost no reach
